panels.visual: A sunny garden outside Athens: Epicurus (gentle, curly beard, simple clothes) with Leontion writing a scroll and the young slave Mys studying, men and women learning together under fig trees; a small sign on the garden gate reads STRANGER, YOU WILL DO WELL TO STAY HERE
panels.caption: Around 306 BC Epicurus bought a garden and taught there. Men, women, even slaves.

panels.visual: A simple table with a loaf of bread, a jug of water and a tiny pot of cheese, Epicurus beaming with delight, a letter beside it
panels.caption: Bread and water make me happy. Send me a little pot of cheese, so that I can have a feast.

panels.visual: Atoms swirling and scattering in a cosmic swirl at the top; below on clouds, the gods lounging bored and uninterested, one yawning, one eating grapes, ignoring the world
panels.caption: Do not fear the gods: they do not meddle with us. Everything is made of tiny atoms.

panels.visual: Epicurus calm with a gentle smile, atoms drifting like dust in a sunbeam, a ribbon with the quote
panels.caption: Do not fear death. When we die, the atoms simply scatter.

speech.speaker: Epicurus
speech.text: Where death is, I am not.

panels.visual: The Agora: rivals whispering behind their hands, pointing at the Garden; in a small inset a Stoic writing and forging rude letters by candlelight with a mean smirk, a pile of fifty letters
panels.caption: Enemies hated that women and slaves were welcome. They spread rumours, and a rival Stoic forged fifty rude letters in his name.

panels.visual: Split image: on the left a cartoon of a huge fat 'Epicurus the glutton' stuffing his face at a banquet, on the right the real Epicurus quietly eating a piece of bread with a cup of water; a bold line between them
panels.caption: They said he overate till he was sick. He lived on bread and water.

panels.visual: A big open dictionary page with the word EPICURE highlighted and a big red stamp reading UNFAIR!, Glauka the owl pointing indignantly at it
panels.caption: The insult stuck: today an epicure means someone who loves rich food.

panels.visual: Old Epicurus sitting in the garden surrounded by his smiling friends, Leontion, Mys and others, warm golden light, his eyes crinkled with a peaceful smile despite a blanket round his legs
panels.caption: He died in 270 BC in great pain, writing to a friend that remembering their conversations made it a happy day.
